newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end up on higher cash ideas.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end up on higher cash ideas.

text.p: Expectations packers will pay $64 per cwt cattle this week combined with fund buying to push CME live cattle futures to higher closes after a prices traded mixed early in response to USDA's Cattle on Feed report, traders said.
Feeder cattle futures also closed higher on fund buying and support from lower corn futures, traders said.
Live cattle ended 0.500 to 0.100 cent per lb higher, paced by August at 64.775 cents. Feeder cattle ended up 0.300 to 0.700 cent with August up 0.475 at 78.750 cents.

The USDA report which showed May marketings in the seven key states at a record 1.8 million head or 104 percent of a year earlier, sparked initial demand in nearby live cattle. A firmer tone in boxed beef prices at noon and expectations packers will pay $64 for fed cattle by the end of the week reinforced buying interest, they said.
"The beef looks like it is turning around toward the firmer side led by the select beef," one trader said.
Packers are cutting kills and putting less beef and pork in the pipeline as they try to firm up the product markets as much as possible, traders added.

Prudential Securities bought August much of the day to bolster the market before profit taking pared best levels late. But buying by Cargill Investor Services and Smith Barney at the close kept the market supported, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, commission houses bought August 66 calls and sold October 70 calls. Commercials did December risk reversals, long 66 puts/short 76 calls, pit sources added.
Feeder cattle futures also ran up from a mixed start on fund buying which touched off buy stops. The rally in back months of live cattle and lower corn futures added to the advance, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.45 at $76.74 per cwt.

ADM Investor Services and Cargill continued to buy August, traders said, and LIT division of First Options bought August early. Cargill also spread long December and February live cattle/short August feeders, pit sources said.
The new boneless beef and beef trimmings contracts traded for the first time Monday. Trade was fairly active with 72 trades in boneless beef and 39 in trimmings.
Boneless beef closed at 89.70 to 93.00 cents per lb and trimmings 43.80 to 41.50 cents.

Commercials generally bought while locals sold. There was also some spreading of long August/short October boneless by seculators. Lind-Waldock notably bought while Fimat Futures USA sold, pit sources said.

The first day of trading started at 1000 CDT and 50 contracts were traded in the first hour. On Tuesday the contracts will start at their normal hours of 0850 CDT/1350 GMT to 1300 CDT/1800 GMT. Options in both markets start trading on Tuesday.

Traders said inaugural trading in the contracts was very good. They looked for increased volume when options start trading and when there is a settlement to base spreading on. There was no limit on the initial day of trade which kept some business on the sidelines until Tuesday, sources said.
